did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with a list of the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua, and it identifies the heads of the priestly families in the days of Jeshua.
Did you know? The Levites were assigned specific duties: some were responsible for thanksgiving and singing, while parallel groups served in rotation.
Did you know? Nehemiah traces a priestly line from Jeshua through Joiakim, Eliashib, and Joiada, to Jonathan and Jaddua.

Did you know? The records of the heads of the Levitical and priestly families were preserved until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib; the priests are also mentioned in connection with the days of Darius, king of Persia.
Did you know? Before the dedication of Jerusalem’s wall, the Levites were gathered from all their towns to celebrate with joy, thanksgiving, singing, and music played on stringed instruments.
Did you know? Before the dedication of the wall, the priests and Levites purified not only the people but also the gates and the wall itself.
Did you know? At the dedication of the wall, two thanksgiving processions traveled in opposite directions along the wall, accompanied by leaders, priests, singers, and musical instruments.
Did you know? The celebration at the dedication of the wall included women and children, and the text emphasizes that the joy of Jerusalem could be heard from far away.

Did you know? After the celebration, men were appointed to oversee the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits, and tithes, so they could collect the portions designated for the priests and Levites.
Did you know? In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel provided daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers, while the Levites set aside their portions for the descendants of Aaron.
